verses.text: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.
His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.
Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”
Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.
Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.

The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; a thing ought not to be done.
Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”
Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.
Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”
The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,
and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised;
then will we give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
But if you will not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our sister,  and we will be gone.”
Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.
Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,

“These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.
Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let us give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
On the third day, when they were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.
They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.
Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,
and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”
They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”

footnotes.content: A young heart goes out to see what lies beyond her own tent. How easily curiosity opens doors we did not mean to walk through, and how much we need the Lord's keeping hand when we do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sin rarely stops at desire; it seizes what it should not. The text says he took her and humbled her. The Lord sees every wrong done to the weak, and He will not forget.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is a difference between love and selfish attachment. Shechem's soul clung to Dinah, yet he spoke kindly only after he had already wronged her. True love longs to protect, not to violate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He treats marriage as a demand to be granted, not a covenant to be earned. How unlike the Lord Jesus, who instead gave Himself to win a bride for Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jacob held his peace. I have learned there are times to speak, and times when a father's grief is so sharp he must wait. Yet the God of justice is never silent over such a thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hamor comes to talk, but words come too late to undo the deed. Still the Lord gives space to speak, though He weighs every word of both sides.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Righteous anger has its place. To see such folly done in Israel grieved and enraged Jacob's sons. But grief must never be left to fester into unrestrained cruelty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hamor speaks of his son's longing, but says little of the young woman's brokenness. The world's way is to plead affection while excusing violence. The Lord cares for the one who has been wronged.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They offer intermarriage to cover over sin. How often men try to make alliances to hush what ought to be judged. God calls for repentance, not cover-ups.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land is large enough for them, but peace bought by pretending the wrong never happened will not last. Our true rest is only in the Lord who makes all things right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shechem offers anything to have her. Wealth can buy many things, but it cannot undo shame or heal a wounded heart. Only the grace of Jesus can truly restore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He is willing to pay a great dowry, yet unwilling to answer for his crime. The heart that loves sin will spare no expense to keep it, but will never count the cost to others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons answer with deceit. Two wrongs never make a right. When we repay evil with evil, we wound our own souls as much as we wound others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They appeal to the reproach of uncircumcision. God's sign to Abraham was meant to mark a people belonging to Him, not a weapon for revenge. How easily holy things are twisted when the heart is bitter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Deceit dressed in religious terms is still deceit. The covenant sign is laid hold of here for guile. The Lord sees through every hidden motive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They speak of becoming one people, while plotting bloodshed. Unity built on falsehood crumbles into ruin. True oneness comes only through the one peace-maker, Jesus Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A threat hides behind their condition. Coerced compliance is no consent at all. The Lord hates violence done under the guise of right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hamor and Shechem are pleased, thinking a bargain is struck. How blind we are when we only count our gain and never reckon with the God who judges.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He hurries to do it for the delight he has in her. Desire that will not wait for righteousness rushes headlong into judgment. I pray the Lord would slow hasty feet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They speak at the gate, where justice should be sought. Instead, guile finds an audience of men eager for their own advantage. Beware of counsel that flatters self-interest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peaceful they say, while plotting treachery. Words are cheap when the heart is crooked. The Lord of truth discerns between honest peace and a snare.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They consent to circumcision for the sake of gain, not for the sake of belonging to God. A sign of covenant used as a price for plunder is an abomination in His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their eyes are on flocks and possessions. They count the spoils before the sword falls. Earthly gain has led many down a road they never meant to take.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the men listen and submit. One bad bargain made at the gate cost an entire city its strength. We are all too quick to follow where self-interest leads.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On the third day, when they are sore and defenseless, Simeon and Levi strike. Vengeance that waits for weakness is cruel indeed. Our God avenges in righteousness; we must leave vengeance to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They kill Hamor and Shechem and bring Dinah home. Justice was needed, but this is massacre. I grieve that a sister's wrong was answered with so much more sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Jacob come upon the dead and plunder. This echoes the way war so often spreads—one act of violence begets another until it devours all. Only the Prince of Peace can break that cruel cycle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They take flocks, herds, donkeys. The very things the men of Shechem boasted would be theirs now belong to those they wronged in return. Greed multiplies grief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wealth, little ones, wives—all taken captive. The cost of deceit and vengeance falls heaviest on the innocent. How thankful I am that Jesus bears the innocent sufferings of His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jacob rightly fears. By their rashness they have made his family a stench to the land. The promise of God to bless still holds, but sin brings needless trouble even for those He has called.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute? Their question sounds zealous for honor, yet it justifies slaughter. True honor guards the weak without trampling mercy. Our hope is only in the righteous Judge who is also our merciful Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
